post:
Sharing rooftop solar between neighbours sounds simple until you have to decide who gets which kilowatt-hour, every 15 minutes, and then bill 34 members fairly.

Swiss local electricity communities (LEG) have been legal since 1 January 2026, so I built an open-source engine for the allocation and billing step. It takes 15-minute meter profiles for consumers and PV plants, allocates the solar energy with three methods (static shares, dynamic by consumption, and a weighted max-min fair one), prices it with 2026 ElCom tariffs, and writes monthly bills, invoices and a metered-data export.

Measured on a simulated community of 34 consumers and 110 kWp of PV for one year:
- Static shares used 44.8% of the PV locally, dynamic and fair allocation 53.8%.
- The energy balance closed with 0 Wh error in all 35,040 intervals.
- With a 40% grid-fee reduction, the median household saves CHF 51 per year, about 6% of its bill.

Not verified: the loads are simulated, not real meter data. The grid-fee reduction comes from secondary sources, so it is a parameter, and the exported message follows the SDAT-CH structure but is not validated against the official schema.

If you run or plan a LEG, which would you want first: simple fixed shares, or the allocation that wastes the least solar?

Code: https://github.com/Usernamepersonperson/leg-allocation-sim
